basis_short: February 2024 procurement prices, national average yields, costs not included
status: provisional — secondary source (USDA FAS Cairo), NOT FAOSTAT; FAOSTAT could not be reached when this file was built
important_caveats: Prices are a single snapshot from February 2024, before the March 2024 devaluation of the Egyptian pound. Absolute EGP values are out of date; use them only to compare crops with each other.
These are government procurement or guaranteed minimum prices, not prices observed on a specific farm.
Yields are national averages, not the yield of the farmer's field.
Revenue = yield x price. It is gross revenue, not profit: no production costs are included.
No price is available for berseem (a forage crop, usually fed on-farm or sold locally) or faba bean. Rotations containing them cannot be given a complete revenue figure.

wheat.yield_source: USDA FAS Cairo, Grain and Feed Update EG2024-0023 (25 Sep 2024), Post estimate MY2024/25
wheat.price_source: USDA FAS Cairo, Sugar Annual EG2024-0011, table 'Government Procurement Prices Announced in February 2024'
wheat.note: Procurement price was raised to 1,900-2,000 EGP/ardeb on 14 Mar 2024 (EG2024-0023).

maize.yield_source: USDA FAS Cairo, Grain and Feed Update EG2024-0023, Post estimate MY2024/25
maize.price_source: USDA FAS Cairo, Sugar Annual EG2024-0011, same table (white corn; yellow corn is 9,500 EGP/t)
maize.note: White corn price used. Yellow corn: 9,500 EGP/t.

rice.yield_basis: milled-equivalent (3.9 MMT milled / 670,000 ha); rough (paddy) yield is 8.4358 t/ha
rice.yield_source: USDA FAS Cairo, Grain and Feed Update EG2024-0023, Post estimate MY2024/25
rice.price_basis: milled rice, market-based (the government does not set a rice procurement price)
rice.price_source: USDA FAS Cairo, Sugar Annual EG2024-0011, same table
rice.note: Farmers sell paddy, not milled rice, so milled yield x milled price overstates farm revenue (it includes the milling margin). Treat as an upper bound. The source table's own per-hectare figure multiplies paddy yield by the milled price and is higher still; it is not used here.

soybean.yield_source: USDA FAS Cairo, Oilseeds and Products Annual EG2024-0008 (4 Apr 2024)
soybean.price_source: USDA FAS Cairo, Sugar Annual EG2024-0011, same table

sunflower.yield_source: implied by the same table (37,500 EGP/ha / 15,000 EGP/t)
sunflower.price_source: USDA FAS Cairo, Sugar Annual EG2024-0011, same table

cotton.yield_source: implied by the same table (288,600 EGP/ha / 200,000 EGP/t)
cotton.price_source: USDA FAS Cairo, Sugar Annual EG2024-0011, same table (Upper Egypt cotton)
cotton.note: Upper Egypt cotton price; Delta (long-staple) prices differ. Season-ending prices in MY2023/24 ranged widely by governorate.

sugar_beet.price_source: USDA FAS Cairo, Sugar Annual EG2024-0011, same table
sugar_beet.note: The source row is internally inconsistent (per-hectare and per-ton figures imply an implausible yield and a different exchange rate). Do not compute revenue until a yield is sourced. Later announcements put the price at 2,300-2,400 EGP/t.

faba_bean.yield_source: secondary summaries citing FAO data (about 3.4-3.5 t/ha); verify

berseem.note: Forage crop; no market price in the sources used. Its value is mostly as livestock feed.
